items.where: Sign-up card, the “First class free” box at the top
items.now: New students try it free. Nothing is due until you decide to stay.
items.proposed: New students try their first class on us. Nothing is due unless your child wants to stay.
items.alt: Come see if it clicks! New students try their first class on us, and nothing is due until you decide to stay.
items.why: Warmer, and uses the home page’s own idea that you only pay if your child wants to stay.

items.where: Sign-up card, heading
items.now: Choose a time
items.proposed: Pick a time that works
items.why: Friendlier heading; the phone bar’s “Choose a time” button stays as it is.

items.where: Sign-up card, main button (both places that set it)
items.now: Continue to enrollment
items.proposed: Sign up for this time
items.why: Plain, friendly words that still say exactly what the button does. “Join waitlist” and “Get notified” are unchanged.

items.where: Sign-up card, the line under the button
items.now: Next you’ll pick your student and pay in our family portal.
items.proposed: Next, you’ll choose who’s coming and pay in your family account.
items.why: Matches the next step’s heading (“Who’s coming”) and the name families see everywhere else (“family account”). The free-class and prorated sentences after it stay word for word.

items.where: Sign-up card when no dates are set yet (camps)
items.now: We announce summer camp a few weeks ahead. Leave your email and we’ll tell you as soon as registration opens.
items.proposed: We announce summer camp a few weeks ahead. Leave your email and you’ll be first to hear when registration opens.
items.why: Echoes the home page’s “Be first to hear about camps.”

items.where: Sign-up card for lessons and parties, heading
items.now: Book it
items.proposed: Let’s plan it
items.why: Sounds like the start of a conversation, which is what the request form is.

items.where: Sign-up card for lessons and parties, text
items.now: Scheduled around your family. Tell us what you have in mind and we’ll get back to you.
items.proposed: We’ll fit it around your family’s calendar. Tell us what you have in mind, and we’ll get back to you.
items.why: A full, warmer sentence with the same promise. The Ovation text is unchanged.

items.where: Under the sign-up card
items.now: Questions? Ask us before you sign up.
items.proposed: Not sure it’s the right fit? Ask us, and we’ll help you pick.
items.why: The home page’s own words; it answers the question parents actually have at this point.

items.where: Bottom of the page, heading above other classes
items.now: You might also like
items.proposed: Your Little Character might also love
items.why: Uses the brand’s own name for students instead of a stock phrase.

groups.title: Step 1: Sign in and who’s coming

items.where: Progress steps at the top of every step, the last one
items.now: Done
items.proposed: All set
items.why: Friendlier finish line; it still reads as the last step.

items.where: Sign-in box, text under “First, who’s signing up?”
items.now: Enter your email and we’ll send a 6-digit code. New here? That’s all it takes to create your family account. This device stays signed in for 90 days.
items.proposed: Enter your email and we’ll send a 6-digit code. New here? That’s all it takes to make your family account, no password needed. This device stays signed in for 90 days.
items.why: Adds “no password needed”, which is true and already said on the other sign-in screen, and takes away a common worry.

items.where: Sign-in box, after the code is sent
items.now: We sent a code to {email}. It expires in 10 minutes.
items.proposed: Check your inbox! We sent a code to {email}. It expires in 10 minutes.
items.why: Tells the parent what to do next, in a friendly way; the 10 minutes stay.

items.where: A date that isn’t open yet
items.now: We haven’t opened registration for this date yet.
items.proposed: We haven’t opened registration for this date yet. Choose “Get notified” and we’ll email you when it opens.
items.why: Points to the button below instead of leaving the parent at a dead end.

items.where: Notice when the class is full
items.now: This class is full. Choose your students to join the waitlist, and we’ll email you if a spot opens.
items.proposed: This class is full right now. Choose your students to join the waitlist, and we’ll email you if a spot opens.
items.why: “Right now” softens the news and is true: spots do open.

items.where: Label beside a child who took the free class
items.now: Trial class taken · continue
items.proposed: Free class done · ready to continue
items.why: Says “free class”, the words families saw when they booked it.

items.where: Age note beside a child outside the class’s ages (the first part comes from the class’s age label and stays exact)
items.now: Ages 7–10. Leo is 5. Ask us if you think it’s still a fit.
items.proposed: Ages 7–10. Leo is 5. Think it’s still a good fit? Ask us.
items.why: Puts the question first so “Ask us” reads as an invitation, not a rule. Ages and age are unchanged.

items.where: First visit, no students saved yet
items.now: Add your first student below.
items.proposed: Add your first student below. We can’t wait to meet them!
items.why: A warm welcome at the very first step of a new family’s sign-up.

items.where: Error when no student is ticked
items.now: Pick at least one student.
items.proposed: Pick at least one student to continue.
items.why: Calm and says why; no joke in an error message.

items.where: Heading
items.now: A few details
items.proposed: A few details for the teachers
items.alt: A few things our teachers should know
items.why: Says who the answers are for, which makes the medical and pickup questions feel less like paperwork.

items.where: Line under the heading
items.now: Enrolling Leo and Mia in Intro to Theater.
items.proposed: Almost there! Enrolling Leo and Mia in Intro to Theater.
items.why: A little encouragement just before the payment step. The heading “Review & pay” stays.

items.where: Payment choice “Try the first class free”, its line
items.now: Nothing due today. Decide after the class.
items.proposed: Nothing due today. See if it clicks, then decide.
items.why: The home page’s own phrase; “Nothing due today” stays exact.

items.where: Line under “You’re in!”
items.now: Leo is enrolled in Intro to Theater. We sent a confirmation to {email}.
items.proposed: Leo is enrolled in Intro to Theater. We can’t wait to meet them! We sent a confirmation to {email}.
items.alt: Leo has joined the cast of Intro to Theater! We sent a confirmation to {email}.
items.why: Celebrates the moment; “enrolled” stays in the first option so nobody wonders whether it worked.

items.where: Heading of the checklist
items.now: Before the first class
items.proposed: Getting ready for the first class
items.why: Reads as a friendly checklist. The items under it (clothes, parking, late arrivals, autopay) stay word for word.

items.where: First line (enrolled, not waitlist)
items.now: Leo is enrolled in Intro to Theater.
items.proposed: Leo is enrolled in Intro to Theater. We can’t wait to meet them!
items.why: Matches the confirmation page (C22). The waitlist line is unchanged.

items.where: Free first class line
items.now: Your first class is free. After it, you can continue with monthly tuition or pay for the season from your family account.
items.proposed: Your first class is free. If it clicks, you can continue with monthly tuition or pay for the season from your family account.
items.why: Same choices and money words, with the site’s “see if it clicks” idea.

items.where: New last line, after the family account link
items.now: (no sign-off)
items.proposed: See you soon! The Little Characters team
items.why: The email ends on a link today; a short sign-off makes it sound like it came from people.
